title: Independent TypeScript readiness findings
summary: Machine-readable findings from the independent runtime, type-system, refiner, packaging, release, and cross-language readiness audit.

items.title: Inconsistent Result discriminator
items.observed_behavior: Guards require exact booleans while match, flatten, transpose, tap, and unwrapOrElse use JavaScript truthiness.
items.impact: Malformed JavaScript or decoded cross-language values can be classified differently by different public operations.
items.remediation: Define exact boolean discrimination and apply it consistently, with an explicit trusted versus decoded input boundary.

items.title: Mutable None singleton
items.observed_behavior: The shared internal None object is returned to consumers without runtime freezing.
items.impact: A JavaScript caller can globally corrupt future Option conversion results.
items.remediation: Use one canonical immutable None representation and verify mutation resistance.

items.title: Duplicated core types
items.observed_behavior: Result and Option definitions are duplicated across public and shared packages with manual synchronization comments.
items.impact: Competing type authorities can drift while tests validate a sibling type instead of the public package type.
items.remediation: Project all duplicate declarations from one canonical contract and add declaration equivalence checks.

items.title: Constructors return wide union
items.observed_behavior: Ok and Err constructors return the full Result union rather than their concrete branch types.
items.impact: Branch certainty is discarded and impossible branches remain visible to TypeScript consumers.
items.remediation: Export named branch types and return the concrete branch from each constructor.

items.title: Underspecified extraction errors
items.observed_behavior: Extraction operations throw generic JavaScript Error values and unwrap discards the rejected error payload.
items.impact: Cross-language exception mapping and diagnostics are unstable.
items.remediation: Define a stable extraction failure category and preserve diagnostic cause where supported.

items.title: Unsound isTypedVariantOf
items.observed_behavior: Object.keys on an erased generic always produces an empty key list while the guard asserts the complete caller-selected payload type.
items.impact: Missing and incorrectly typed payload fields are accepted as type-safe.
items.remediation: Require explicit runtime validators or keys and limit inferred output to facts established at runtime.

items.title: Refiners accept missing payload
items.observed_behavior: Configured payload keys are skipped when validators are absent and their presence is never independently checked.
items.impact: Returned types claim required fields that do not exist at runtime.
items.remediation: Require own-property presence for every configured payload and infer concrete types only from validators.

items.title: Variant controls are ignored
items.observed_behavior: Public strictFields and forbidden configuration fields are not read by any refiner implementation.
items.impact: Consumers can mistake successful refinement for strict schema or security-boundary validation.
items.remediation: Define and implement own-field strictness and forbidden-field semantics in a shared validation kernel.

items.title: Variant matchers lose handlers
items.observed_behavior: Strict matcher resets on every subsequent handler and non-strict matcher resets after the second handler.
items.impact: Apparently registered branches fall through or throw at runtime.
items.remediation: Use a builder factory that closes over the complete immutable accumulated handler list.

items.title: Strict exhaustiveness is reversed
items.observed_behavior: Handled extends all variants becomes true after any one valid branch instead of when no variants remain.
items.impact: Strict run is available before exhaustive handling.
items.remediation: Enable run only when Exclude of all variants by handled variants is never.

items.title: Matcher output is unknown
items.observed_behavior: Both matcher factories fix their return type to unknown and discard handler result inference.
items.impact: Consumers lose useful static types after a fully typed match.
items.remediation: Accumulate handler output types and narrow fallback input to unhandled variants.

items.title: Inconsistent property ownership
items.observed_behavior: Some refiners require own type fields while others accept inherited discriminators, variants, payloads, and validators.
items.impact: Prototype properties can be treated as schema members and invoked as validators.
items.remediation: Use own-property checks for discriminators, payloads, configuration variants, and validators.

items.title: Validator output types are erased
items.observed_behavior: ValidatorFn carries a predicate target but refined result aliases ignore it and emit unknown fields.
items.impact: Runtime validation provides no corresponding developer type benefit.
items.remediation: Derive synchronous payload types from predicate targets and explicitly model asynchronous validator output.

items.title: Never sentinel collision
items.observed_behavior: The payload string never is indistinguishable from an ordinary string field after widening and collides with a real field named never.
items.impact: Configuration inference and cross-language representation are fragile.
items.remediation: Use an empty payload-key list in the canonical model and retain the string only as a deprecated projection input.

items.title: Sync and async refiner drift
items.observed_behavior: Sync and async variants have duplicated implementations, different output precision, and no async full-map counterpart.
items.impact: Behavior and declarations can diverge across equivalent entry points.
items.remediation: Use a shared validation model and document intentional capability differences.

items.title: Clean release build is broken
items.observed_behavior: Package and root release commands reference local build and release scripts that are ignored or absent from tracked files.
items.impact: CI and release verification cannot succeed from a clean checkout.
items.remediation: Track required release tooling and add packed-package consumer tests from a clean environment.

items.title: Canonical contract layer is absent
items.observed_behavior: The documentation framework references language-neutral contracts, registries, and core governance files that do not exist.
items.impact: No auditable source of truth or cross-language conformance baseline exists.
items.remediation: Create this strict machine-readable Contract IR corpus and bind implementations through projections and evidence.

items.title: Type contract tests are absent
items.observed_behavior: Runtime Vitest tests do not provide compile-negative declaration conformance and often import the sibling shared type.
items.impact: Unsound guards, exhaustiveness failures, and inference regressions can ship undetected.
items.remediation: Add package-root positive and expected-error compile fixtures against packed declarations.
